_comment: GRC-parity block target manifest. Machine-readable source of truth for the status dashboard and the agent work-queue. Edit this (status, grc_block, params, notes); metrics are filled from verification reports by tools/gen_dashboard.py. Do NOT hand-edit STATUS.md. status: done | in_progress | planned | wont_map. tier: 1=feed-forward (autonomous), 2=stateful/loop, 3=new GRC block to build. Priority is tier-ascending then listed order.
_naming_principle: Names must match GNU Radio so users never guess the equivalent. (1) Each Kyttar block's GRC palette LABEL is its GNU Radio counterpart's label verbatim (e.g. 'FIR Filter'), keeping a 'Kyttar'/'kyttar_' marker ONLY where GRC namespacing requires it to coexist with stock GR. (2) 'grc_block' below names the EXACT GNU Radio factory (e.g. filter.fir_filter_fff) so the equivalence is explicit and searchable in the dashboard. A Kyttar block with no clean GNU Radio counterpart sets grc_block to '' and explains in notes.

blocks.notes: Reference example; fully documented. Single MULQ.

Complex (I/Q) fixed-gain scaler — the 2-rail twin of GainBlock, scaling both rails by the SAME real constant (no rotation). Supports gain in (0,4) via integer-doubling (ADD) + Q15 fractional (MULQ) so the datapath stays Q15 while gain>1. Receiver gain-staging: restores the ~2.8x the 16-QAM matched filter's Q15 headroom pre-scale attenuates, before the fixed-threshold DD Costas/slicer. Verified on-chip (0.3 -> 0.78 exact) and load-bearing in the shipped qam16_modem BER-0 example; NOT yet through per-block GRC-equivalence verification.

Zero-stuffing rate expander (front half of an interpolating pulse-shaper). Verified 1:1 vs interp_fir_filter_fff(sps,[1.0]): one input -> sample + sps-1 zeros, kept sample pass-through, zeros exact -> bit-exact in Q15. RATE-EXPANDING: verified with run_block_dut_rate (drains the full per-trigger burst; plain run_block_dut keeps only the last word). 9 tests (sps in {2,4,8}, full-scale edges, repeat-instead-of-zero + wrong-rate mutations). Single cell, unrolled WRITE/JUMP burst then HALT (JUMP does NOT halt the issuer).

Hold-upsampling rate expander (each input emitted interp times) — the symbol-HOLD a shaped-envelope TX needs between its mapper and an envelope stage (PSK31's RaisedCosineEnvelope consumes a HELD ±A stream; the zero-stuffing UpsamplerBlock would feed it zeros). Verified 1:1 vs blocks.repeat(sizeof_float, interp): pure pass-through, bit-exact in Q15. RATE-EXPANDING (run_block_dut_rate). 11 tests (interp in {1,2,4,8}, full-scale edges, zero-stuff/wrong-rate/inverted/empty mutations, interp>8 raises — unrolled single-cell budget guard). Saturated-stream gate green (RATE_1IN).

Complex (I/Q) zero-stuffing rate expander — the 2-rail twin of UpsamplerBlock and the front half of a complex interpolating pulse-shaper (feed into ComplexRRCMatchedFilter as a shaper). Verified 1:1 vs interp_fir_filter_ccc(sps,[1+0j]): one complex input -> sample + sps-1 (0,0) pairs, kept sample pass-through on BOTH rails, zeros exact -> bit-exact in Q15. Each output is a yi/yq PACKET (WRITE yi; WRITE yq; JUMP) — the complex-packet contract (INV-17). 12 tests (sps in {2,3,4}, full-scale edges, bit-exact ref, repeat/swapped-IQ/wrong-rate/empty mutations). HARDWARE LIMIT: sps<=4 single cell (3-word packet halves the real block ceiling of 8); sps>4 RAISES (guard test). QPSK modem uses sps=2.

Now takes GR real-world params sample_rate + frequency (Hz); derives the 16-bit freq_word internally (freq_word=round(freq/samp*65536)) — was exposing the raw hardware freq_word proxy. GR equivalent = multiply_cc(baseband, sig_source_c(samp,COS,freq,1,0,ph0)) -> complex_to_real, ph0=2pi*freq/samp (increment-before-emit). 1 LSB vs GR, delay 0. 11 verify + 25 build/catalog tests. Q15 overflow corner (|I|+|Q|>1 WRAPS) verified vs own ref. Migrated the build/catalog/verify tests off freq_word.

Matches firdes.root_raised_cosine(gain,sampling_freq,symbol_rate,alpha,ntaps) VERBATIM via a bit-exact firdes port in _firdes.root_raised_cosine (max dev ~1e-8 across gain/fs/alpha/ntaps). Taps run on the verified FIR datapath; sps derived from sampling_freq/symbol_rate (was hardcoded 4). 15 tests: tap-parity, BPSK stream, impulse, alpha+ntaps+gain sweeps, inverted+wrong-alpha mutations. Old hand-rolled alpha/span formula removed.

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.multiply_ff (N-stream, num_inputs param). out[n]=a0[n]*a1[n]*...*a(N-1)[n] -- the element-wise product of num_inputs real streams (default 2). GR multiply_xx exposes num_inputs (the number of input ports), so this block MIRRORS it with a num_inputs param: N inputs land in R0..R(N-1) and the product is a chain of MULQ (out=((a0*a1)>>15*a2)>>15...). HARDWARE LIMIT: num_inputs<=24 (the N input registers + chained MULQ must fit one 32-word cell); raises loudly above (and on <2). Distinct from GainBlock (multiply by a CONSTANT) and ComplexMixerBlock (multiply by an internally-generated complex exponential). Verification: N=2 via run_block_dut_complex (a/b carried as one complex array); N=3,4 via run_block_dut_nstream (N-operand fan-in: WRITE a0..a(N-1), JUMP). Two-tier: DUT vs GR multiply_ff with N connected ports (AMPLITUDE, ~1 LSB/MULQ) AND DUT vs process_reference_q15 (EXACT, the chained wrapping Q15 MULQ). Q15 OVERFLOW: the lone 2-input overflow is (-1.0)*(-1.0)=+1.0 where MULQ WRAPS to -1.0 (datapath wraps, not saturates) -- a dedicated test asserts DUT==wrapping reference. Multiply is COMMUTATIVE (swapped-stream mutation not a corruption, documented); inverted/wrong-second-stream/halved/+1-delay/empty mutations all FAIL (INV-4). num_inputs-over-limit raises (tested).

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.add_ff (N-stream, num_inputs param). out=a0+a1+...+a(N-1) of num_inputs real streams (default 2). GR add_xx exposes num_inputs (input-port count), so this block MIRRORS it: N inputs in R0..R(N-1), chained pairwise saturating ADD. HARDWARE LIMIT: num_inputs<=6 (the per-step saturating add chain + emit must fit one 32-word cell); raises loudly above (and on <2). PRODUCTION SATURATION (not wrap): the Q15 ALU ADD WRAPS on overflow (0.6+0.6 -> -0.8 sign flip), a footgun; this block SATURATES each step like the FIR/dc-blocker. Mechanism: ADD sets V; on overflow rail from the saved accumulator's sign via SHR#15;ADD satpos (+0x7FFF/-0x8000). The chain stays straight-line with FORWARD BR.NV +N skips (the FIR's idiom; a back-jump/GOTO onto a {write}/{jump} placeholder is miscompiled). Verification: N=2 via run_block_dut_complex; N=3,4 via run_block_dut_nstream. Two-tier: DUT vs GR add_ff with N connected ports (AMPLITUDE, IN-RANGE stimulus amp~0.9/N so the N-way sum stays representable where saturate==true sum, ~1 LSB) AND DUT vs process_reference_q15 (EXACT, chained saturating add). Saturation verified directly (N=3 overflow pins to +-full, no wrap). num_inputs-over-limit raises (tested). Add is COMMUTATIVE. Shares add_block.py with SubtractBlock.

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.sub_ff (N-stream, num_inputs param). out=a0-a1-...-a(N-1) of num_inputs real streams (default 2; matches GR sub: a0 minus all the rest). Same single-cell chained SATURATING combiner as AddBlock (shares add_block.py / _NStreamAddSub) with SUB instead of ADD; the per-step rail is picked from the saved accumulator sign (same SHR#15;ADD satpos restore). HARDWARE LIMIT num_inputs<=6, raises above (and on <2). Verification N=2 (run_block_dut_complex) + N=3,4 (run_block_dut_nstream); two-tier vs GR sub_ff with N connected ports (AMPLITUDE, in-range) AND vs process_reference_q15 (EXACT, chained saturating sub). N=3 overflow saturates to -full (tested, no wrap). Subtract is NOT commutative (a-b!=b-a) so a swapped-stream mutation IS a corruption and is tested, plus inverted/wrong-second-stream/+1-delay/empty. num_inputs-over-limit raises. add_cc/sub_cc (complex, 4 external operands) deferred to Tier-2.

Verified BIT-EXACT vs GNU Radio blocks.xor_bb (2-input byte XOR). out = a ^ b of two byte (uint8) streams. Single cell: ONE native LOGIC XOR (R0 = R0 ^ R1, which writes R0), then emit -- the LOGIC-op twin of MultiplyBlock (same 2-in fan-in a@R0/b@R1, single ALU op, R0 out). PURE BITWISE: no Q15, no rounding, no saturation, no overflow corner -- a byte 0..255 rides the low 8 bits of the 16-bit word and XOR is bit-parallel, so the on-chip result is bit-exact for the WHOLE 8-bit byte. GR xor_bb takes 2+ streams; this block maps the canonical 2-input case (num_inputs pinned to 2 in the GRC binding). VERIFICATION SUBSTRATE NOTE: bytes are RAW words, NOT Q15 -- the shipped run_block_dut_* drivers quantise operands via _to_q15(float) (byte 170 -> 0x7FFF), and compare_against_grc saturates the reference as Q15 floats (255.0 -> 0x7FFF) + its DECISION metric compares only the packed LSB. So test_xor.py uses a bespoke RAW-word 2-input driver (same proven place/route/build/hop path, but inject_data_physical of raw bytes) and a DIRECT byte-for-byte equality gate (all 8 bits), which is strictly stronger than DECISION. Coverage: named edges (0^0, 0xFF^0xFF, 0xFF^0x00, 0xAA^0x55, 0x0F^0xF0, ...), 5 random seeds vs LIVE xor_bb, own process_reference_bytes, D4 orientation-invariance (INV-23: emitting orientations bit-exact). INV-4 proven at the SUBSTRATE level: a real on-chip AND-instead-of-XOR block is caught by the gate (7/7 bytes differ); plus AND/OR/drop-input-a/drop-input-b/inverted/+1-delay/empty mutations all FAIL. 33 tests green. GRC binding kyttar_xor (byte in/out). add_cc/and_bb/or_bb siblings deferred.

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.complex_to_float (re=real(in), im=imag(in); 20 tests shared with FloatToComplexBlock). On the Kyttar substrate a complex sample IS a two-operand (re@R0, im@R1) pair, so this conversion is the IDENTITY datapath: read the pair, emit it as two words (re then im) on one bus corridor, de-interleaved by the harness into I/Q (the NCO/mixer two-word-egress pattern). Pure data movement (MOVE/WRITE, NO arithmetic) so it is EXACT -- zero Q15 error -- and the gate is bit-exact (metric=exact) on BOTH channels. Single cell, words_per_sample=2. Mutations (swapped re/im, negated imag/conjugate, +1 delay, empty) all FAIL (INV-4). Shares _IQPassthrough/complex_float_block.py with FloatToComplexBlock.

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.float_to_complex (out=re+j*im of two real streams). The complement of ComplexToFloatBlock and the SAME identity datapath (shares _IQPassthrough/complex_float_block.py): the two real inputs (re@R0, im@R1) are emitted as the two words of one complex sample. EXACT, bit-exact gate on both channels, single cell, words_per_sample=2. The complex<->float pair is the most common type conversion in any I/Q graph. Mutations (swapped re/im, negated imag, +1 delay, empty) all FAIL.

Verified BIT-EXACT vs LIVE GNU Radio blocks.float_to_char(scale): out = saturate_int8(round_half_even(in*scale)), a signed int8 in [-128,127] emitted as one raw-integer word (the slicer output convention, NOT a Q15 fraction). Single cell, feed-forward. Datapath on the Q15 input k (in=k/32768): q = MULQ(k,scale) = (k*scale)>>15 (arithmetic floor); r = MUL(k,scale) masked to low 15 bits = (k*scale) mod 2^15; round-half-to-EVEN bumps q iff r>2^14 OR (r==2^14 AND q odd) -- matches GR's lrintf/np.rint default FE_TONEAREST tie-to-even, NOT round-half-up (a half-up DUT is a proven-failing mutation); then int8 saturation. Sample is saved to a state reg first (input lands at R0 = accumulator, so MULQ would clobber it before the second MUL -- the one real bug found+fixed). HW-DEVIATION (INV-0): scale must be a NON-NEGATIVE INTEGER (GR takes an arbitrary float scale); a non-integer/negative scale can't reproduce the exact-tie rounding bit-for-bit so the block RAISES (documented in __init__ comment, class docstring, and here). Input domain = the whole Q15 range [-1,1) (GR is driven with the SAME quantised value the chip sees). Verified: edge + random (3 seeds) x scale sweep {1,2,64,127,128,200}, exact round-half-even ties (k*scale=2^14*(2m+1)), and +/-full-scale saturation to +127/-128, all BIT-EXACT (11k+ offline points 0 mismatch; on-chip vs live GR 0 mismatch). Mutations truncate-not-round, round-half-UP-not-even, wrap-not-saturate, wrong-scale, 1-sample-shift, empty all FAIL (INV-4). Orientation-invariant (all 8 D4) + pipeline-saturation (REAL_1IN) green. GRC binding: kyttar_float_to_char.block.yml + float_to_char.py shim (preview np.rint == GR, bit-exact), snake->Pascal importer mapping (no override needed).

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.complex_to_mag_squared (out=re^2+im^2; 21 tests). The instantaneous-power / envelope primitive (energy detectors, AGC error, squelch). Single cell, two Q15 ops: MULQ re,re then MACQ im,im accumulate (re^2+im^2) in R0. No params (full GRC parity). SATURATION: the power range [0,2) overflows Q15's [0,1) for |z|>=1 (the unit circle), so the block SATURATES to +full-scale. The power is ALWAYS >=0, so any overflow makes the 16-bit accumulator look negative (bit15 set) -- detected with a single BR.N and pinned to 0x7FFF (a cheaper one-sided clamp than the add/sub sign-rail; no satpos sign math needed). Two-tier: DUT vs GR (AMPLITUDE, IN-RANGE |z|<1 where the result is representable, op_count=2 floor=3 LSB, measured ~2 LSB from MULQ/MACQ truncation vs GR's rounded square) AND DUT vs process_reference_q15 ((re^2>>15)+(im^2>>15) saturating, EXACT, incl. overflow corners). Saturation verified directly (|z|>=1 pins to +full, no wrap). |z|^2 is SYMMETRIC in re/im so a swapped-channel mutation is not a corruption (documented); mutations inverted/halved/wrong-second-stream/+1-delay/empty all FAIL (INV-4). complex_to_mag (sqrt) and complex_to_arg (atan2) of backlog #4 are DEFERRED to Tier-2 (need new sqrt/CORDIC machinery -- see TIER1_BLOCK_BACKLOG).

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.conjugate_cc (out=conj(in)=re-j*im; 11 tests). The correlator / conjugate-multiply staple. Single cell: pass re through, negate im (0-im via SUB), emit the two words; words_per_sample=2. No params (full GRC parity). EXACT gate (0 LSB vs GR on both channels) -- pure data movement + one negate. Q15 corner: the only imag whose negate overflows is exactly -1.0 (0x8000): -(-1.0)=+1.0 is unrepresentable so SUB WRAPS to 0x8000 (the bit-exact reference models the wrap; a dedicated test pins it). GR-equivalence stimulus stays off im=-1.0 so the conjugate is exact. Key mutation (teeth): a NOT-conjugated DUT (im passed through un-negated) FAILS -- proves the block actually conjugates, not echoes; plus swapped-channels/+1-delay/empty all FAIL (INV-4).

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.abs_ff (out=|in|; 9 tests). Single cell, one conditional negate (CMP vs 0, then 0-in if negative -- the AGC/QAM16-slicer abs idiom; BR.NN target on a REAL instruction). Single real input via run_block_dut, single real output. No params (full GRC parity). Result is EXACT (0 LSB vs GR) except the lone in=-1.0 (0x8000) corner: |-1.0|=+1.0 unrepresentable so the negate WRAPS to 0x8000=-1.0 -- the bit-exact reference models the wrap (a dedicated test pins it) and the GR-equivalence stimulus stays off it. Key mutation (teeth): a NON-rectified DUT (a negative passed through) FAILS, proving the block takes the magnitude; plus +1-delay/empty FAIL (INV-4). NOTE the backlog #7 'negate' (unary sign flip) is GainBlock(gain=-1) -- already covered, not a separate block; analog.rms_cf is deferred to Tier-2 (needs the deferred Q15 sqrt + a stateful averager).

Explicit 1-cell stream fan-out relay (GRC id kyttar_splitter; the plain SplitterBlock name is the LEGACY duplex landing cell) (out = in on every arm), verified EXACT vs blocks.copy (test_splitter.py: edge/random/bit-exact + value-corruption, offset, empty mutations). Authored with a RESERVED exit tail (14 HALT words) so the build's single-rail fan-out form (_patch_single_rail_multi_handoff) can grow up to 8 WRITE+JUMP arm pairs in place; splitters tree for wider fan-outs. The GRC importer AUTO-SPLICES one wherever a flowgraph fans a single-rail block output to >=2 different blocks or >=3 inputs (and behind a chip input port fanning ONE stream to >=3 blocks); a same-target 2-arm fan-in stays direct (packet form). Whole-chain proofs incl. the Add/Multiply COUNTING JOIN (fires on last arrival, any arm order): test_fanout_chains.py.

Verified BIT-EXACT vs LIVE GNU Radio blocks.and_const_bb (out = in & constant on an unsigned-byte stream; 29 tests). Single cell, one LOGIC.AND of the input register against a baked immediate -- the AddConst/Gain single-cell-op-with-baked-constant shape, but bitwise (no Q15 rounding path), so the DUT matches GR bit-for-bit over the whole 0..255 byte range. 'constant' mirrored VERBATIM; applied as constant & 0xFF. Byte data rides simKYT as raw uint16 words (0..255 all positive) and is compared as INTEGERS via the byte/32768.0 round-trip into _saturate_ref_q15. METRIC: the gate is Metric.EXACT (full-word array_equal, tol 0), NOT DECISION -- DECISION compares only the LSB (a & 1) and MISSES an upper-bit error (proven: 128->0 passes DECISION, fails EXACT), so a wrong-constant mutation on the upper bits would slip past DECISION; EXACT is the only valid bit-exact gate for a full byte (manifest 'metric' field records the block's decision/byte class). Coverage: edge (constant=0 all-zeros, 0xFF identity, 1 LSB, 0x0F nibble), random>=3 seeds, constant sweep (11 masks), orientation-invariant across all 8 D4, mutations FAIL (OR-instead-of-AND, wrong constant, identity/unmasked, +1-delay, empty). GR-VERSION FINDING: this GNU Radio build rejects a constant outside 0..255 (both -1 and 256 raise) -- and_const_bb's constant is an UNSIGNED byte here, not a signed char, so the block's &0xFF mirror is faithful (a guard test pins it).

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.keep_one_in_n (keep 1 sample of every n, no filter; 26 tests). A pure pass-through gated by a modulo-n counter -- the DecimatorBlock's emit gate WITHOUT the FIR. Single cell. Param mirrors GR: n (keep factor). PHASE: GR keeps the LAST sample of each group of n (verified empirically: keep_one_in_n(3) of 0..11 -> 2,5,8,11 = phase n-1), so the up-counter emits when it reaches n then resets (XOR self), matching GR. EXACT pass-through (no Q15 arithmetic) -> bit-exact gate; emitted samples equal the input bit-for-bit. run_block_dut records None on dropped triggers so the kept stream is outputs[n-1::n]; the emit-phase contract (emit iff i%n==n-1) is asserted directly across n in {1..5}. Mutations (wrong n, wrong phase n-2, +1 delay, empty) all FAIL (INV-4). Counter is a persistent StateVar (init 0); the skip path is a bare HALT label (a REAL instruction, not a {write}/{jump} placeholder -- build-engine GOTO miscompile). repeat (the upsampling twin) and interleave/deinterleave deferred to Tier-2 (see TIER1_BLOCK_BACKLOG).

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.delay (integer-sample delay line; 28 tests). y[n]=x[n-delay]: prepend 'delay' zeros then the input stream unchanged (no filter, no interpolation -- a pure time shift). Param mirrors GR VERBATIM: delay (integer sample delay, default 1). Single cell: a delay-deep shift register held in state registers d0..d(delay-1) (oldest at d0=x[n-delay], newest at d(delay-1)=x[n-1]), ALL initialised to Q15 0 -- which IS the prepended zeros. Per trigger: save the oldest, shift the line down (d0<-d1..d(D-2)<-d(D-1)), push the input at the tail, emit the saved oldest. Pure data movement (MOVE only, NO Q15 arithmetic) -> EXACT (0 LSB vs GR), metric=exact. REGISTER-ALLOC TRAP (the real bug found+fixed): with no data words the free register gap STARTS at reg 0, so an auto-allocated d0 landed ON the input reg 0 (=R0) and every trigger emitted the RAW input un-delayed (an echo, delay ignored). Fix: PIN the delay line + save reg to registers 1..delay+1 so they never overlap the input reg 0 (mirrors how KeepOneInN's data words push state off 0). ALIGNMENT (INV-2): a delay is a KNOWN non-zero shift, asserted the RIGHT way -- an impulse lands at index 'delay' and ONLY there, dut[:delay]==0 and dut[delay+k]==x[k] vs the RAW input (not a free lag). Two-tier: DUT vs LIVE GR blocks.delay bit-exact over delay 1..8 + 3 random seeds + max depth (both streams carry the prepended zeros, compared delay=0 since GR also emits [0]*delay+x); AND DUT vs process_reference_q15 (EXACT). Edge: delay=0 identity, delay=1, delay=MAX. Mutations +1-extra-delay, no-delay-passthrough, advance-instead-of-delay, wrong-delay, empty all FAIL (INV-4). Orientation-invariant in all 8 D4 (added to test_orientation_invariance) + saturation-safe (no feedback / no reconvergent fan-in; added to test_pipeline_saturation). HW-DEVIATION (INV-0, RAISES never clamps): the delay line + shift program must fit ONE 32-word cell, so the depth is capped at MAX_DELAY=12 (empirically delay=13 builds but emits no output -- osave overflows into the instruction region; delay=14 raises). GR blocks.delay is unbounded (host RAM); a deeper on-chip delay needs a fabric FIFO / multi-cell line (Tier-2). GRC: kyttar_delay.block.yml label 'Delay' + kyttar.delay shim; grc_import resolves kyttar_delay->DelayBlock via snake->Pascal fallback.

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.moving_average_ff (out=scale*sum of last `length` samples; 18 tests). A moving average IS an FIR whose `length` taps are all equal to `scale`, so MovingAverageBlock SUBCLASSES the verified FIRFilterBlock with constant box taps (the LowPassFilter pattern) -- all Q15 datapath / multi-cell fold / COEFFICIENT-HEADROOM saturation inherited unchanged. Constant taps are symmetric so the reversed-tap convention is moot and group delay=0, aligned with GR's causal running sum. Params mirror GRC's Moving Average: length + scale (GR's max_iter is an output-buffer bound and vlen=1 -- neither affects the sample math, so neither is a Kyttar param). scale=1/length is a true average (Sum|tap|=1 -> S=0); a larger scale engages the inherited saturating headroom restore (S>0). Two-tier: DUT vs GR moving_average_ff (AMPLITUDE, headroom-aware q15_quant_floor(length,S)) AND DUT vs the inherited process_reference_q15 (EXACT). Coverage: edge + 3 random + length sweep {2,3,5,8,16} (true average) + bit-exact incl. S=1 headroom (3,0.5)/(6,0.3); mutations inverted/wrong-length/+1-delay/empty all FAIL (INV-4). KNOWN LIMIT (inherited FIR per-cell budget): a SINGLE-cell box with S>0 caps at ~3 taps -- a 4-tap box at scale 0.5 (4 taps + S=1 restore on one cell) raises at build; use scale<=1/length (S=0) or a longer/multi-cell length. Not a moving-average-specific limit.

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.complex_to_real (out=real(in); 18 tests shared with ComplexToImagBlock). A complex sample is carried as a two-operand (re@R0, im@R1) pair; this selector forwards the RE operand as its single real output (words_per_sample=1). A subset of complex_to_float but a separate GR block people wire directly to grab one rail. Pure data movement (one MOVE) -> EXACT (0 LSB vs GR). No params. Single cell, shares _ComplexSelect/complex_real_imag_block.py with ComplexToImagBlock. Key mutation (teeth): selecting the WRONG rail (real DUT vs GR imag reference) FAILS, proving it picks the correct channel; plus +1-delay/empty FAIL (INV-4).

Verified vs GNU Radio blocks.complex_to_imag (out=imag(in)). The IM-channel twin of ComplexToRealBlock and the SAME selector datapath (shares _ComplexSelect/complex_real_imag_block.py): forwards the im operand (R1) as the single real output. EXACT (0 LSB), single cell, words_per_sample=1. Mutations (wrong rail = imag DUT vs GR real, +1-delay, empty) all FAIL.

Verified vs filter.dc_blocker_ff. GR's DC blocker is LTI -- a SYMMETRIC FIR -- so DCBlockerBlock SUBCLASSES the verified FIRFilterBlock with the dc-blocker impulse response as its coefficients. Reverse-engineered from GR impulse/step response and confirmed bit-for-bit (float, <1e-4) for D in {2,4,8,16,32}, both forms: SHORT form (long_form=False) = x[n-(D-1)] - MA_D^2(x) (two cascaded length-D moving averagers; triangular kernel, 2D-1 taps, group delay D-1); LONG form (long_form=True, GR default) = x[n-(2D-2)] - MA_D^4(x) (four cascaded; 4D-3 taps, group delay 2D-2). Sum(taps)=0 (true DC notch); taps symmetric so the FIR reversed-tap convention is moot. Params mirror GR's GRC dc_blocker_xx VERBATIM: length (GR's D, default 32) + long_form (default True). GR default = 125 taps = 26 cells; folds 7x4 (<=8 across, INV-9), routes + sims + matches GR end-to-end. TOLERANCE: the dc-blocker taps have Sum|h|~1.5..2, so COEFFICIENT HEADROOM (INV-13) engages with S=1 (coeffs pre-scaled by 1/2, saturating-shift gain restore -> the block SATURATES on overload, no rollover). S=1 costs ~1 bit of coeff precision, so the DUT-vs-GR amplitude floor is the HEADROOM-AWARE q15_quant_floor(N, head_shift=S) = N*(2^(S-1)+1)+1 LSB (=2N+1 at S=1), NOT the plain N+1 -- a DERIVED fixed-point worst case (empirically bounds the error with ~18% margin), not a loosened gate. Two-tier verification like the FIR: DUT vs GR float (amplitude, headroom floor) AND DUT vs process_reference_q15 (EXACT, models the saturating datapath). Coverage: taps-vs-GR-impulse, edge + 3 random + (length,long_form) sweep single->26 cells, bit-exact multicell, overload-saturation (sign-aligned full-scale pins the rails) + wrap-mutation, and inverted/wrong-length/+1-delay/empty/deep-cell mutations all FAIL the gate. Fixed a latent FIR _fold_geometry bug (n=26 had only the H=1 even-column fold -> a 26x1 off-grid LINE; capped even-column folds to <=8 across, INV-9) and extended INV-11 params-threading to the GUI port-stub/flyline renderer (chip_canvas resolved port geometry param-less, dropping a scaling block's last-cell output stub). QUARANTINE (re-attempted 2026-08-27; still needs_human, but the 2026-08-06 root cause was WRONG). The documented cause (TED precision: the >>1 halving) is NOT the limit: an ablation on the same channel/metric shows removing it reaches only BER 0.0122 (2/50 cases failing). The ACTUAL defect is an UNBOUNDED PHASE ACCUMULATOR - the Q14 NCO has no modulo, so whenever the loop pulls the period below nominal phase grows without bound and WRAPS int16 (measured 32298), inverting the interpolation: the loop SLIPS rather than jitters. Replacing it with the MMTimingRecovery modulo-1 counter (cnt=(cnt-W)&0x7FFF), plus GR-derived PI gains (the >>8/>>2 shifts are ~12.8x too weak) and a full-precision MULQ TED (+2 bits, needed for cold acquisition), gives BER 0 on ALL 50 selection cases AND 200 held-out cases in a bit-exact Q15/ISA model. It does NOT ship because the redesign does not close its feedback loop ON-CHIP: the block places/routes/builds, egresses at the correct rate, and ted.cprev matches the reference, but period_relay never executes so counter.v stays 0. The wall is a BUILD-INTEGRATION one - a single cell cannot reliably be both the external-egress cell and an internal feedback-trigger source (four build passes contend for the exit cell WRITE/JUMP words). See lessons_log 2026-08-27 for the ablation table, the ring-parity fact (the 5-cycle needs a transit cell), the transit-face overwrite hazard, and the concrete next step. VERIFIED alternative for this channel remains MMTimingRecoveryBlock.

blocks.notes: DONE (wave 7, joint build with SqrtBlock; FULL cost recorded here). placeKYT-NATIVE ordered two-word rendezvous -- NO GNU Radio counterpart exists because the problem does not exist in GR (its scheduler aligns two input streams). THE PROBLEM, measured on real hardware: a downstream cell consuming a FIXED-ORDER pair through ONE input port + ONE entry (the toggle-cell contract, e.g. GRUCellBlock's fin) cannot be fed by two nets into that entry -- it BUILDS AND ROUTES ok=True and SILENTLY produces garbage, reading the two streams as word0/word1 of ALTERNATING timesteps and HALVING the rate. _elect_join_triggers declines to arbitrate when the target declares only an EntryPoint; the counting join is explicitly ORDER-FREE (wrong primitive for a fixed order); broker coalescing collapses two nets into N WRITEs + ONE JUMP into the same in_reg (second overwrites first); DualFloatToComplexBlock has the right rendezvous but emits a 2-rail packet with ONE trigger (wrong output SHAPE). MECHANISM: INPUT = the Dual's LOCK-BY-FACE rendezvous verbatim (face IS the stream identity; NEEDS_DISTINCT_INPUT_FACES; cold-start initial_lock_face so there is no arm-JUMP race). OUTPUT = TWO SEQUENTIAL WRITE+JUMP bursts from a SINGLE-RAIL cell. NO RAW_OUTPUT_HOPS and NO hand-routing were needed (investigated, not required): the ordinary single-net patcher _patch_cell_handoff already sets EVERY WRITE and EVERY JUMP in the cell to the SAME (hop, dest, entry), which turns the authored 4-instruction emit into exactly two independent deliveries of one downstream entry. Two conditions keep that path live and BOTH are asserted by the suite: (a) exactly ONE output register (>1 would classify it as a COMPLEX 2-rail source and collapse the bursts into a consecutive-register packet with one trigger), (b) the output cell carries no internal handoff and no WRITE.CFG (so _output_cell_carries_handoffs stays False and BOTH bursts are patched, not just the last WRITE/JUMP). ENGINE FIX shipped with it: _apply_rendezvous_input_faces hardcoded the Dual's port/word names ('i'/'q', face_i/face_q), so for ANY other rendezvous block it was a SILENT NO-OP -- the LOCK gated the authored placeholder faces, the real arms were barred, and the chain built + routed perfectly while emitting ZERO output. Generalized to a block-declared RENDEZVOUS_FACE_PORTS (the Dual now declares its historical names explicitly; its 8 tests stay green). VERIFIED ON CHIP, 32 tests, EXACT tol 0 -- every proof is a REAL two-upstream chain (two independently rate-reducing KeepOneInN arms -> join), placed + routed + built and run on the simulator, never a single-block proxy: ORDER (a always first) for A-then-B, B-then-A (byte-identical streams), bursty arms, and RANDOM per-timestep order over 3 seeds x 10 timesteps; arms with DIFFERENT decimation rates (n=2 vs n=4) still pair emission-for-emission -- the join pairs EMISSIONS, not raw samples; back-to-back timesteps never mix (even positions are a-words, odd are b-words); STARTUP emits nothing until both arms speak (no partial pair); a STARVED arm yields exactly one pair and RECOVERS with the correct partner when the missing word arrives. THE END-TO-END GATE: the whole chain 2 arms -> join -> GRUCellBlock (the REAL single-port toggle consumer, 51 cells) -> x16_out on ONE 10x12 chip produces class words BIT-IDENTICAL to feeding that same consumer the ordered pairs directly ([0,1,1,0,0,0] both ways), at the CORRECT rate -- 6 pairs in -> 6 words out, pinning the rate-halving failure mode. A >1-INPUT-REGISTER CONSUMER ALSO WORKS -- measured, correcting an earlier code-read assumption that it would not: the complex-abutment patcher sets the hop on every WRITE/JUMP but the dest only on WRITE index rail_idx, which for a net into the consumer's FIRST input is 0 while the second burst's WRITE already carries that dest, so the outcome equals _patch_cell_handoff (gated on chip against an AddBlock a0 by test_target_with_multiple_input_registers_still_gets_two_bursts). KNOWN LIMIT (explicit guard, AGENTS.md section 6): an arm may run at most TWO timesteps ahead; at depth 3 the surplus words are LOST (the arm's producer wedges and the chain emits nothing even after the other arm catches up).
